import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder
from IPython.display import display

# Load Car Evaluation Dataset
url = 'https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data'
column_names = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
df = pd.read_csv(url, names=column_names)

# Features to encode
features = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety']
X_cat = df[features]

# OneHotEncode (compatible with any sklearn version)
encoder = OneHotEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(X_cat)
if not isinstance(X_encoded, np.ndarray):
    X_encoded = X_encoded.toarray()  # Convert sparse matrix to dense numpy array if needed

# Standardize encoded features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_encoded)

# Generate 10 random seed sets of 3 unique indices
np.random.seed(42)
all_indices = np.arange(X_scaled.shape[0])
seed_sets = [np.random.choice(all_indices, size=3, replace=False) for _ in range(10)]

for i, seed_indices in enumerate(seed_sets, start=1):
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"SEED SET {i}: {seed_indices}")
    
    # Initial centroids from seed indices
    initial_centroids = X_scaled[seed_indices]
    
    # KMeans clustering (3 clusters)
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init=initial_centroids, n_init=1, random_state=43)
    cluster_labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)
    
    df_temp = df.copy()
    df_temp['Cluster'] = cluster_labels
    
    # Create count matrix of true class vs cluster
    count_matrix = pd.crosstab(df_temp['class'], df_temp['Cluster'], margins=True, margins_name='Total')
    total_counts = count_matrix.loc['Total']
    
    # Calculate percentages
    percentage_matrix = count_matrix.div(total_counts).mul(100).round(1)
    
    # Combine counts and percentages
    combined_matrix = count_matrix.copy().astype(str)
    for col in count_matrix.columns:
        for idx in count_matrix.index:
            count = count_matrix.loc[idx, col]
            percent = percentage_matrix.loc[idx, col]
            combined_matrix.loc[idx, col] = f"{count} ({percent}%)"
    
    print(f"\nCLASS-CLUSTER DISTRIBUTION MATRIX FOR SEED SET {i} (Seeds: {list(seed_indices)})")
    print("(Format: Count (Percentage%))\n")
    display(combined_matrix.style.set_caption(f"Seed Set {i} - Class vs Cluster Distribution"))
    
    # Display count matrix with gradient
    print("\nCount Matrix with Gradient Coloring:")
    styled_counts = count_matrix.style.background_gradient(
        cmap='Blues',
        subset=pd.IndexSlice[count_matrix.index.drop("Total"), count_matrix.columns.drop("Total")]
    )
    display(styled_counts)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder
from IPython.display import display

# Load Car Evaluation Dataset
url = 'https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data'
column_names = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
df = pd.read_csv(url, names=column_names)

# Features for clustering (categorical)
features = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety']
X_cat = df[features]

# OneHotEncode features
encoder = OneHotEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(X_cat)
if not isinstance(X_encoded, np.ndarray):
    X_encoded = X_encoded.toarray()  # convert sparse to dense if needed

# Standardize features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_encoded)

# Define 10 different seed sets of initial indices (randomly chosen, 3 seeds each)
np.random.seed(42)
all_indices = np.arange(X_scaled.shape[0])
seed_sets = [np.random.choice(all_indices, size=3, replace=False) for _ in range(10)]

# Initialize lists to store all count and percentage matrices
all_count_matrices = []
all_percentage_matrices = []

for i, seed_indices in enumerate(seed_sets, start=1):
    df_temp = df.copy()
    initial_centroids = X_scaled[seed_indices]
    
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init=initial_centroids, n_init=1, random_state=1)
    df_temp['Cluster'] = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)
    
    # Count matrix: true class vs predicted cluster (no margins)
    count_matrix = pd.crosstab(df_temp['class'], df_temp['Cluster'])
    
    # Percentage matrix: proportion per cluster (sum per cluster = 100%)
    percentage_matrix = count_matrix.div(count_matrix.sum(axis=0), axis=1).mul(100).round(1)
    
    # Store matrices
    all_count_matrices.append(count_matrix)
    all_percentage_matrices.append(percentage_matrix)

# Calculate average counts and percentages across all seed sets
avg_count_matrix = pd.concat([m.stack() for m in all_count_matrices], axis=1)\
                    .mean(axis=1).unstack().round().astype(int)
avg_percentage_matrix = pd.concat([m.stack() for m in all_percentage_matrices], axis=1)\
                         .mean(axis=1).unstack().round(1)

# Create combined average matrix
combined_avg_matrix = avg_count_matrix.copy().astype(str)
for col in avg_count_matrix.columns:
    for idx in avg_count_matrix.index:
        count = avg_count_matrix.loc[idx, col]
        percent = avg_percentage_matrix.loc[idx, col]
        combined_avg_matrix.loc[idx, col] = f"{count} ({percent}%)"

# Add totals (counts only, percentages not meaningful for totals)
combined_avg_matrix['Total'] = avg_count_matrix.sum(axis=1).astype(str)
total_row = avg_count_matrix.sum(axis=0).astype(str)
total_row['Total'] = str(avg_count_matrix.values.sum())
combined_avg_matrix.loc['Total'] = total_row

# Display the average results
print(f"\n{'='*80}")
print("AVERAGE CLASS-CLUSTER DISTRIBUTION ACROSS ALL 10 SEED SETS")
print("(Format: Average Count (Average Percentage%))")
print(f"{'='*80}\n")

styled_avg = combined_avg_matrix.style.set_caption(
    "Average Distribution Across All Seed Sets"
).set_table_styles([
    {'selector': 'caption', 'props': [('font-size', '16px'), ('font-weight', 'bold'), ('text-align', 'center')]},
    {'selector': 'th', 'props': [('text-align', 'center')]},
    {'selector': '.row_heading, .col_heading', 'props': [('font-weight', 'bold')]},
])
display(styled_avg)

# Also display numeric average matrices separately
print("\nAverage Count Matrix:")
display(avg_count_matrix)

print("\nAverage Percentage Matrix:")
display(avg_percentage_matrix)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler

# Load Car Evaluation Dataset
url = 'https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data'
column_names = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
df = pd.read_csv(url, names=column_names)

# OneHotEncode categorical features for clustering
features = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety']
X_cat = df[features]
encoder = OneHotEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(X_cat).toarray()

# Standardize features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_encoded)

# Define 10 random seed sets (3 indices each)
np.random.seed(42)
all_indices = np.arange(X_scaled.shape[0])
seed_sets = [np.random.choice(all_indices, size=3, replace=False) for _ in range(10)]

# For each seed set, run kmeans and print combined count + % table
for idx, seed_indices in enumerate(seed_sets, start=1):
    df_temp = df.copy()
    initial_centroids = X_scaled[seed_indices]

    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init=initial_centroids, n_init=1, random_state=42)
    df_temp['Cluster'] = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)

    count_matrix = pd.crosstab(df_temp['class'], df_temp['Cluster'])

    # Calculate percentage per cluster (column-wise)
    col_sums = count_matrix.sum(axis=0).replace(0, np.nan)
    percentage_matrix = (count_matrix.div(col_sums, axis=1) * 100).round(1).fillna(0)

    # Combine count and percentage in one table
    final_table = pd.DataFrame()
    for cluster in sorted(count_matrix.columns):
        final_table[f'Cluster {cluster}'] = count_matrix[cluster].astype(str) + ' (' + percentage_matrix[cluster].astype(str) + '%)'

    # Row totals: sum counts and row % of total samples
    row_counts = count_matrix.sum(axis=1)
    row_percents = (row_counts / len(df) * 100).round(1)
    final_table['Total'] = row_counts.astype(str) + ' (' + row_percents.astype(str) + '%)'

    # Column totals: sum counts and % of total samples
    col_counts = count_matrix.sum(axis=0)
    col_percents = (col_counts / len(df) * 100).round(1)
    total_row = [f"{col_counts[c]} ({col_percents[c]}%)" for c in count_matrix.columns] + [f"{len(df)} (100.0%)"]
    final_table.loc['Total'] = total_row

    # Print nicely
    print("=" * 100)
    print(f"SEED SET {idx}: {seed_indices}")
    print("Class-to-Cluster Distribution (Format: Count (Percentage%))")
    print("=" * 100)
    print(final_table.to_string())
    print("\n\n")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder, StandardScaler
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

# Load Car Evaluation Dataset
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
df = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Encode categorical features and target into numeric values
le = LabelEncoder()
df_encoded = df.apply(le.fit_transform)

# Separate features and labels
X = df_encoded.iloc[:, :-1]  # all features except class
y = df_encoded['class']       # class column (optional)

# Standardize features for clustering
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

# Apply KMeans clustering (choose number of clusters, e.g., 4 for car classes)
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, n_init=10, random_state=42)
labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)

# Create co-occurrence matrix: 1 if same cluster, else 0
co_occurrence = np.equal.outer(labels, labels).astype(int)

# Convert to DataFrame with sample labels S0 to S1727 (since dataset has 1728 rows)
co_matrix_df = pd.DataFrame(co_occurrence,
                            index=[f"S{i}" for i in range(len(labels))],
                            columns=[f"S{j}" for j in range(len(labels))])

print("=== Co-occurrence Matrix for Car Evaluation Dataset Clusters ===")
print(co_matrix_df)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OrdinalEncoder

# Load Car Evaluation dataset
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
car_data = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Take first 500 data points
car_data_subset = car_data.iloc[:500]

# Encode categorical features
encoder = OrdinalEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(car_data_subset)

# Standardize the features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_encoded)

# Define 10 different seed index sets (3 points each)
seed_sets = [
    [5, 55, 105]
]

# Dictionary to hold all co-occurrence matrices
co_occurrence_matrices = {}

# Generate co-occurrence matrix for each seed set
for i, seed_indices in enumerate(seed_sets, start=1):
    # Initialize centroids from selected seed indices
    initial_centroids = X_scaled[seed_indices]
    
    # Run KMeans with these centroids
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init=initial_centroids, n_init=1, random_state=42)
    labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)
    
    # Co-occurrence: 1 if same cluster, else 0
    co_occurrence = np.equal.outer(labels, labels).astype(int)
    
    # Store in dictionary as DataFrame
    co_occurrence_matrices[f"Seed Set {i}"] = pd.DataFrame(
        co_occurrence,
        index=[f"S{j}" for j in range(500)],
        columns=[f"S{j}" for j in range(500)]
    )

# Print all 10 matrices (or just the first matrix preview to avoid huge output)
for seed_name, matrix in co_occurrence_matrices.items():
    print(f"\n=== Co-occurrence Matrix for {seed_name} (showing first 10x10) ===")
    print(matrix.iloc[:500, :500].to_string())

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OrdinalEncoder

# Load Car Evaluation dataset
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
car_data = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Take first 500 data points
car_data_subset = car_data.iloc[:500]

# Encode categorical features (excluding class label if you want)
encoder = OrdinalEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(car_data_subset.iloc[:, :-1])  # exclude class from features

# Standardize the features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_encoded)

# Define 10 different seed index sets (3 points each)
seed_sets = [
    [5, 55, 105]
]

# Dictionary to hold all co-occurrence matrices
co_occurrence_matrices = {}

for i, seed_indices in enumerate(seed_sets, start=1):
    initial_centroids = X_scaled[seed_indices]

    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init=initial_centroids, n_init=1, random_state=42)
    labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)
    
    # Calculate cluster sizes
    unique_labels, counts = np.unique(labels, return_counts=True)
    cluster_size_dict = dict(zip(unique_labels, counts))
    max_size = counts.max()

    # Create matrix where co-occurrence = scaled cluster size * 10 if same cluster else 0
    co_occurrence = np.zeros((500, 500), dtype=float)
    for a in range(500):
        for b in range(500):
            if labels[a] == labels[b]:
                size = cluster_size_dict[labels[a]]
                scaled_value = (size / max_size) * 10  # scale to 0-10 range
                co_occurrence[a, b] = scaled_value
            else:
                co_occurrence[a, b] = 0

    # Store as DataFrame
    co_occurrence_matrices[f"Seed Set {i}"] = pd.DataFrame(
        co_occurrence,
        index=[f"S{j}" for j in range(500)],
        columns=[f"S{j}" for j in range(500)]
    )

# Print first 10x10 values of first seed set matrix as preview
print("=== Preview of Co-occurrence Matrix with scaled cluster sizes (Seed Set 1) ===")
print(co_occurrence_matrices["Seed Set 1"].iloc[:100, :100].to_string())

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OrdinalEncoder

# Load Car Evaluation dataset
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
car_data = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Take first 500 data points
car_data_subset = car_data.iloc[:500]

# Encode categorical features (excluding class label)
encoder = OrdinalEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(car_data_subset.iloc[:, :-1])  # exclude 'class'

# Standardize the features
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_encoded)

# Define 10 different seed index sets (3 points each)
seed_sets = [
    [5, 55, 105]]

co_occurrence_matrices = {}

for i, seed_indices in enumerate(seed_sets, start=1):
    initial_centroids = X_scaled[seed_indices]

    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, init=initial_centroids, n_init=1, random_state=42)
    labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)
    
    unique_labels, counts = np.unique(labels, return_counts=True)
    cluster_size_dict = dict(zip(unique_labels, counts))
    max_size = counts.max()

    co_occurrence = np.zeros((500, 500), dtype=int)  # int dtype now
    for a in range(500):
        for b in range(500):
            if labels[a] == labels[b]:
                size = cluster_size_dict[labels[a]]
                scaled_value = int(round((size / max_size) * 10))  # integer value 0-10
                co_occurrence[a, b] = scaled_value
            else:
                co_occurrence[a, b] = 0

    co_occurrence_matrices[f"Seed Set {i}"] = pd.DataFrame(
        co_occurrence,
        index=[f"S{j}" for j in range(500)],
        columns=[f"S{j}" for j in range(500)]
    )

# Preview 10x10 for first seed set
print("=== 10x10 Preview Co-occurrence Matrix (integers 0-10) for Seed Set 1 ===")

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
import numpy as np

# Load data
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
car_data = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Encode categorical features (exclude target variable 'class')
X = car_data.drop('class', axis=1)
encoder = OrdinalEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(X)

# Take 10% of the data points (~173 rows)
sample_size = int(0.10 * len(car_data))
X_sample = X_encoded[:sample_size]

# Apply KMeans clustering (4 clusters)
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42)
clusters = kmeans.fit_predict(X_sample)

# Build co-occurrence matrix
n = len(clusters)
co_occurrence = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=int)

for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        if clusters[i] == clusters[j]:
            co_occurrence[i, j] = 1

# Create DataFrame with labels S0, S1, ...
labels = [f"S{i}" for i in range(n)]
co_occurrence_df = pd.DataFrame(co_occurrence, index=labels, columns=labels)

# Print the co-occurrence matrix
print(co_occurrence_df)

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

# Load Car Evaluation dataset
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
car_data = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Separate features and target
X = car_data.drop('class', axis=1)
y_true = car_data['class']

# Encode categorical features into ordinal numbers
encoder = OrdinalEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(X)

# Run KMeans clustering (choose 4 clusters since 4 classes)
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, n_init=10, random_state=42)
cluster_labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_encoded)

# Create summary table comparing true labels to clusters
summary_df = pd.crosstab(index=y_true, columns=cluster_labels,
                         rownames=["True Label (Class)"], colnames=["Cluster"])

# Make sure cluster columns are 0 to 3
summary_df = summary_df.reindex(columns=range(4), fill_value=0)

# Add totals
summary_df['Total'] = summary_df.sum(axis=1)
summary_df.loc['Total'] = summary_df.sum()

print("=== True Labels vs Clusters (Car Evaluation Dataset) ===")
print(summary_df)

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder

# Load the Car Evaluation dataset
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
car_data = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Separate features and target
X = car_data.drop('class', axis=1)
y_true = car_data['class']

# Encode categorical features
encoder = OrdinalEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(X)

# Run KMeans for 10 seeds (0 to 9)
for seed in range(10):
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, n_init=10, random_state=seed)
    cluster_labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_encoded)

    # Create cross-tab of true labels vs clusters
    summary_df = pd.crosstab(index=y_true, columns=cluster_labels,
                             rownames=["True Label (Class)"], colnames=["Cluster"])

    # Ensure all cluster columns (0 to 3) are present
    summary_df = summary_df.reindex(columns=range(4), fill_value=0)

    # Add row and column totals
    summary_df['Total'] = summary_df.sum(axis=1)
    summary_df.loc['Total'] = summary_df.sum()

    print(f"\n=== True Labels vs Clusters (Car Dataset, Seed = {seed}) ===")
    print(summary_df)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder

# Load Car Evaluation dataset
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
car_data = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Separate features and target
X = car_data.drop('class', axis=1)
y_true = car_data['class']

# Encode categorical features
encoder = OrdinalEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(X)

# Step 1: Create a co-consensus matrix by running KMeans multiple times
n_runs = 10
n_clusters = 4
n_samples = X_encoded.shape[0]
consensus_matrix = np.zeros((n_samples, n_samples))

# Run KMeans multiple times and update co-assignment frequencies
for seed in range(n_runs):
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, n_init=1, random_state=seed)
    labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_encoded)
    for i in range(n_samples):
        for j in range(n_samples):
            if labels[i] == labels[j]:
                consensus_matrix[i, j] += 1

# Normalize the consensus matrix to range [0, 1]
consensus_matrix /= n_runs

# Step 2: Treat each row of consensus_matrix as a data point and apply KMeans
kmeans_final = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, n_init=10, random_state=42)
cluster_labels = kmeans_final.fit_predict(consensus_matrix)

# Step 3: Summary table (True Label vs Cluster)
summary_df = pd.crosstab(index=y_true, columns=cluster_labels,
                         rownames=["True Label (Class)"], colnames=["Cluster"])
summary_df = summary_df.reindex(columns=range(n_clusters), fill_value=0)

# Add totals
summary_df['Total'] = summary_df.sum(axis=1)
summary_df.loc['Total'] = summary_df.sum()

# Display the result
print("=== True Labels vs Clusters (from Consensus Matrix, Car Dataset) ===")
print(summary_df)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier, plot_tree
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, accuracy_score
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder

# === Step 1: Load and prepare the Car Evaluation dataset ===
url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/car/car.data"
columns = ['buying', 'maint', 'doors', 'persons', 'lug_boot', 'safety', 'class']
car_data = pd.read_csv(url, names=columns)

# Encode categorical features
X = car_data.drop('class', axis=1)
y_true = car_data['class']
encoder = OrdinalEncoder()
X_encoded = encoder.fit_transform(X)

# === Step 2: Generate consensus matrix ===
n_runs = 10
n_clusters = 4
n_samples = X_encoded.shape[0]
consensus_matrix = np.zeros((n_samples, n_samples))

for seed in range(n_runs):
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, n_init=1, random_state=seed)
    labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X_encoded)
    for i in range(n_samples):
        for j in range(n_samples):
            if labels[i] == labels[j]:
                consensus_matrix[i, j] += 1

# Normalize to [0, 1]
consensus_matrix /= n_runs

# === Step 3: Final clustering based on consensus matrix ===
kmeans_final = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, n_init=10, random_state=42)
cluster_labels = kmeans_final.fit_predict(consensus_matrix)

# === Step 4: Decision Tree to predict clusters ===
dtree = DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=42)
dtree.fit(consensus_matrix, cluster_labels)

# Predict and evaluate
y_pred = dtree.predict(consensus_matrix)
print("\nDecision Tree Accuracy:", accuracy_score(cluster_labels, y_pred))
print("\nClassification Report:\n", classification_report(cluster_labels, y_pred))

# === Step 5: Plot decision tree ===
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 8))
plot_tree(dtree,
          feature_names=[f"Sample {i+1}" for i in range(consensus_matrix.shape[1])],
          class_names=[f"Cluster {i}" for i in range(n_clusters)],
          filled=True, rounded=True)
plt.title("Decision Tree Predicting Clusters from Consensus Matrix Features (Car Evaluation Dataset)")
plt.show()
